source.title: DataRx: Missingness-Aware Sampling for Safer Large Language Model Task-Specific Fine-Tuning
source.authors: Jun-Bo Zhang; Qian-Li Zhou; Xin-Yang Deng; Wen Jiang

page_placements.theme: Data composition and training objectives shape safety erosion

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether benign task-specific fine-tuning affects harmful-prompt compliance, using task-specific fine-tuning and ASR results rather than the original benign instruction-fine-tuning setup.
record.gate_note: Tests V2 with task-specific fine-tuning on downstream task data. It does not fine-tune on harmful examples. The paper's discussion of shallow alignment and early response tokens cites prior work; this study does not measure token-position KL or test compliant prefills, suffixes, or decoding changes. Safety-data-mixing results concern a mitigation intervention, not whether ordinary benign fine-tuning erodes safety, and are not included as rows for these versions.
record.test_reason: Measures harmful-prompt ASR before and after ordinary benign task-specific LoRA fine-tuning (seven tasks, three instruct models). This is a new setting, task-specific rather than instruction fine-tuning, with a direct result on V2. The authors frame it as a challenge to Eiras et al.'s claim that benign task fine-tuning is safe. No harmful-data fine-tuning, token-position, prefill or localization experiments are run.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that benign task-specific fine-tuning can unintentionally weaken safety, especially with weak initial safety or aggressive learning rates, contradicting Eiras et al. They then propose DataRx, a representation-based selection of safety examples to mix in, as a mitigation.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses LoRA task-specific fine-tuning on seven downstream datasets, for one epoch at learning rates 2 × 10−5 and 2 × 10−4. It does not reproduce harmful-example fine-tuning or general benign instruction fine-tuning; LoRA rank is 16.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported safety degradation varies with learning rate, model's initial safety capability, and downstream task. In the mitigation experiments, the paper also reports variation by safety dataset and safety-data mixing ratio.

fits_no_version.finding: Mixing randomly sampled BeaverTails safety data, or the longest-response safety samples, into task data raised ASR above downstream-only. Llama3 went from 20.24 to 59.23 (random) and 50.19 (Longest); Qwen2.5 went from 19.06 to 50.08 (random).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adding noisy or long-response safety data during fine-tuning can increase harmful compliance rather than reduce it.

fits_no_version.finding: Higher learning rates also gave higher downstream accuracy, so users have an incentive to pick the setting that erodes safety more.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign fine-tuning's safety cost covaries with the hyperparameters that maximize task utility.

record.problems: The learning-rate comparison in Fig. 2 is not numerically reported in the text; the listed table ASRs are post-fine-tuning values without matching pre-fine-tuning values under the same aggregate measure. The ASR judge is Llama-Guard-3-8B, and no uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: None. Tables II and III repeat the same downstream-only ASRs under the two safety-dataset table layouts; those duplicate downstream-only results are recorded once per model and task.

untested.parts: General instruction fine-tuning (e.g. Alpaca/Dolly) and carefully selected benign data are not tested; only downstream task datasets are used, all with LoRA r=16 for one epoch.
No prefill, suffix or decoding attacks.
No test of why alignment is shallow; shallowness is only invoked to explain the Longest-selection result.

missing.what: Pre-fine-tuning (Origin) ASR per benchmark for each model, needed as the baseline for R4–R24
missing.locator: Fig. 4 'Origin' bars; Section II RQ1 text gives DirectHarm4 values 12.75 / 9.5 / 65.5

missing.what: Per-model, per-task ΔASR at lr 2e-5 vs 2e-4 (only plotted, trend given in text)

record.verdict_notes: Row baselines were absent in the record, but Fig. 4 Origin bars, which match the text's initial DirectHarm4 ASRs, supply them. Values are approximate from figure text extraction. Table II and III downstream-only rows are identical; one copy is enough. The ASR judge is Llama-Guard-3-8B, with no uncertainty reported. Mitigation and ablation results were rightly excluded as rows.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples is tested.

Tests benign task-specific downstream fine-tuning, not ordinary instruction fine-tuning or carefully selected benign instruction data. The learning-rate comparison is described in text, but its individual plotted values are not stated numerically.
No per-token KL divergence or other measure of aligned-versus-base output differences across response positions.
No compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes are tested.
LoRA fine-tuning is used, but the study does not test whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
The study does not test whether data or training objectives cause safety to be shallow.
The study does not train or evaluate methods intended to spread safety beyond early response tokens.

labels.label: limits_scope
labels.condition: Conservative lr 2e-5, especially for the more safety-robust models
labels.reason: Restrict this condition group to the more safety-robust Llama3 and Qwen2.5 low-rate settings in R1–R2. Section II explicitly reports substantial Mistral degradation even at 2e-5 (R3), so conservative learning rate alone does not define a uniformly limited-effect group.

relation.reason: Section II directly measures safety degradation from benign task-specific fine-tuning; it also evaluates mitigation.

tranche.reason: Tests V2 in the new setting of benign task-specific LoRA fine-tuning across seven downstream tasks, with before/after harmful-prompt ASR.

source_check.notes: Fig. 4 supplies untreated benchmark baselines; distinguish calculated means from directly reported means. reader_labels.reason: The authors report that increasing the learning rate substantially enlarges the safety alignment gap for all three models and most tasks (R1–R3). The text also reports substantial degradation for Mistral at 2 × 10−5 (R3).
